# dtcloud_lb_pool (Resource)

Manages the back-end pool attached to a listener, and how it spreads connections across its members.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "dtcloud_lb_pool" "web" {
  lb_id       = dtcloud_lb.public.id
  listener_id = dtcloud_lb_listener.https.listener_id

  backend_protocol      = "HTTP"
  backend_protocol_port = 8080
  lb_algorithm          = "ROUND_ROBIN"

  # Pin a client to the member it first reached.
  sticky_session = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `backend_protocol` (String) Protocol used to reach the members. One of: HTTP, HTTPS, TCP, UDP. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `backend_protocol_port` (Number) Port used to reach the members. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `lb_algorithm` (String) Balancing algorithm. One of: LEAST_CONNECTIONS, ROUND_ROBIN, SOURCE_IP. Can be changed in place.
- `lb_id` (String) ID of the load balancer this pool belongs to. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `listener_id` (String) ID of the listener that feeds this pool. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.

### Optional

- `sticky_session` (Boolean) Whether to pin a client to the member it first reached. Can be changed in place.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp as reported by the API.
- `health_monitor_id` (String) ID of the health monitor attached to this pool, if any.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `member_ids` (List of String) IDs of the members currently in the pool.
- `name` (String) Name assigned by the platform.
- `operating_status` (String) Operating status.
- `pool_id` (String) ID of the pool on its own, without the load balancer prefix.
- `provisioning_status` (String) Provisioning status.
- `updated_at` (String) Last-update timestamp as reported by the API.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String)
- `delete` (String)
- `update` (String)

## Behaviour worth knowing

* **Only `lb_algorithm` and `sticky_session` change in place.** The protocol, the port and the owning
  listener are fixed at creation.
* **`sticky_session` is write-only.** The pool list does not report it, so drift in it is invisible
  and it does not survive an import.
* **The algorithm comes back as a display name.** The API answers `Round robin` where it was given
  `ROUND_ROBIN`; the provider maps it back so an imported pool does not look like it needs replacing.

## Timeouts

`create`, `update` and `delete` each default to 15 minutes.

## Import

```shell
# <load-balancer-id>:<pool-id>
terraform import dtcloud_lb_pool.web 3d372446-4c75-4327-9511-98442456162f:5b2a9c31-7e04-4d88-9c6e-44a2f1d0e7b3
```
